review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas, attributes, simprocs or simp sets. Its theorems are one-off existence and membership results: charP_residueField, exists_poly_coeff_not_dvd, exists_pow_sub_one_mem_maximalIdeal, inv_notMem_of_not_isUnit, inv_mem_maximalIdeal_of_notMem, algebraMap_mem_iff_of_gaussPresentation, algebraMap_mem_igusaRing_iff, and solution. Their statements have existential or iff forms with side conditions. None is a rewrite rule that would make a sound simp lemma, so I found no missing canonical simp lemma, no competing rules, no unwanted expansion and no credible cycle. The proofs use simp only in a few places, and those calls are explicit and bounded. I also checked ModularCurve.algebraMap_laurentSeries_eq_single, which the file uses through rw. It is used in rw form in other files, and nothing showed that a simp attribute would help. Without running Lean, I can't tell whether any of the plain simp calls are fragile. I saw no evidence that they are.
